findings.finding: PRD-mandated Session status `changes_ready` is absent from ALL three state machines (SOM §12, UX §8.1, DATA_MODEL §4.1). PRD SESS-3 (functional-requirement ground truth) lists 17 session statuses including `changes_ready`; the three state machines all list 16 and omit it. This is the 'Session 15 vs 16' drift, and it is not a cosmetic count mismatch — it is a missing PRD-required state that flows depend on.
findings.evidence: PRD §10.4 SESS-3 (lines 940-956) enumerates: creating, starting, active, thinking, running_command, editing_files, running_tests, waiting_on_permission, waiting_on_human, waiting_on_external_service, idle, stale, failed, changes_ready, completed, archived, killed (=17). SOM §12 (594-609)=16, UX §8.1 (514-529)=16, DATA_MODEL §4.1 (496)=16 — none contain `changes_ready`. Flow H (UX §10 lines 1980-1981 / PRD §9.9 line 656) is literally 'Session reports/says changes ready'; UX Screen 4 (line 903) lists a 'Completed session with summary' but the changes-ready-before-review state has no enum. UX §5.1 attention order and PRD §5.2 priority order both rank 'changes ready' (#5) as a distinct attention bucket the session list must sort by (PRD SESS-4).
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §5 (Domain Model) / the binding Session state machine: add `changes_ready` as a Session status between the runtime/waiting states and terminal `completed`. Define its entry transition (harness reports work-complete-pending-review, e.g. Claude ResultMessage / Codex turn-end → SessionStatusChanged) and exit transitions (→ active on agent resume, → completed on archive/PR, → failed). Add it to proj_session.status's allowed set and to the attention-ordering projection. Reconcile the count note on DATA_MODEL §2.3 line 142 ('16 states' → 17).

findings.finding: The Approval state machine (DATA_MODEL §4.7) is internally inconsistent across SOM §30, UX §8.7, ACTION_GATEWAY §9.5, and DATA_MODEL §4.7 — and it improperly conflates Approval-lifecycle states with ActionRequest-execution states. DATA_MODEL §4.7 drops three approval outcomes the PRD/AG/EM mandate (`edited`, `auto_approved_by_policy`, `escalated`) and absorbs execution states (`executing/succeeded/failed`) that belong to the ActionRequest, not the Approval.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL §4.7 (line 514): requested→previewed→awaiting_approval→approved|denied|expired|cancelled→executing→succeeded|failed. SOM §30 Approval (1580-1586): requested, approved, denied, EDITED, AUTO_APPROVED_BY_POLICY, expired, ESCALATED. AG §9.5 Approval.status (line 548): requested|approved|denied|expired|cancelled ONLY (no executing/succeeded — those are ActionResult). UX §8.7 (617-630) adds partially_succeeded, rollback_available, rolled_back. The dropped states are load-bearing: AG-3 (PRD line 1492) requires policy auto-approval → needs `auto_approved_by_policy`; Flow G + AG §14.4 (line 1027) allow 'edit instruction' before approve → needs `edited`; EM §10.12 emits `ApprovalEscalated` and HIQ-2 lists 'agent team escalations' → needs `escalated`.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §5: SPLIT into two reconciled machines. (1) Approval lifecycle = {requested, previewed, awaiting_approval, approved, denied, edited, auto_approved_by_policy, expired, cancelled, escalated} — terminal at the decision, mapping to proj_approval_queue.status + approvals.status. (2) ActionRequest/execution lifecycle owns {executing, succeeded, failed, partially_succeeded, rolled_back, rollback_failed} on action_requests.status. Pick AG §9.5 + SOM §30 union as canonical for Approval; pick AG §8 / EM §10.12 ActionExecution* as canonical for execution. Remove execution states from §4.7 Approval enum.

findings.finding: The ActionRequest state machine has 4-way unreconciled drift (SOM §31 vs AG §8 vs DATA_MODEL §2.9 vs EM §10.12 events) and is never listed among 'the 8 state machines' even though every mutation in the system passes through it. There is no single canonical ActionRequest lifecycle in DATA_MODEL §4, only an ad-hoc CHECK-constraint enum buried in the table sketch.
findings.evidence: SOM §31 (1638-1646): draft, preview_ready, awaiting_approval, approved, executing, succeeded, failed, cancelled, rolled_back. AG §8 (384-396): Drafted→Submitted→Normalized→Validated→RiskClassified→Previewed→AwaitingApproval→Approved/Denied/Expired/Cancelled→Queued→Executing→Succeeded/Failed/PartiallySucceeded→RolledBack/RollbackFailed/Archived (19). DATA_MODEL §2.9 action_requests.status (line 437): requested, previewed, policy_decided, awaiting_approval, executing, succeeded, failed, rolled_back (8) — uses `requested` not `draft/submitted`, adds `policy_decided`, drops `denied/cancelled/partially_succeeded/queued`. None match. EM §10.12 implies ActionRequestCreated/ActionPreviewGenerated/PolicyDecisionRecorded/ApprovalRequested/.../ActionExecutionSucceeded as the event-driven transitions. DATA_MODEL §4 has machines 4.1-4.8 but ActionRequest is NOT among them despite being the spine of AG §15.1.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §5/§6: promote ActionRequest to a 9th first-class state machine and bind action_requests.status to the AG §8 lifecycle (collapse internal steps as needed but keep observable states: submitted, previewed, policy_decided, awaiting_approval, approved, denied, expired, cancelled, queued, executing, succeeded, failed, partially_succeeded, rolled_back, rollback_failed). Map each transition to its EM §10.12 authoritative event so the projector can validate. Reconcile the §2.9 CHECK enum to match.

findings.finding: ExecutionProfile §4.8 cites SOM §15 as canonical but its enum does not match SOM §15 at all. DATA_MODEL §4.8 / UX §8.8 use {available, active, in_use, rate_limited, auth_expired, misconfigured, disabled, unknown}; SOM §15 uses {not_configured, ready, auth_expired, rate_limited, disabled, degraded}. `ready/not_configured/degraded` (SOM) vs `available/misconfigured/unknown` + new `active/in_use` (DM/UX) are silently different vocabularies with no mapping.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL §4.8 (line 516-517) header says '[LOCKED — SOM §15, UX §8.8]' but lists available|active|in_use|rate_limited|auth_expired|misconfigured|disabled|unknown. SOM §15 (781-786): not_configured, ready, auth_expired, rate_limited, disabled, degraded. SOM has `degraded` (dropped by DM); DM has `active`, `in_use`, `unknown` (absent in SOM); SOM `ready` ≈ DM `available`; SOM `not_configured` ≈ DM `misconfigured` (different meaning — not-yet-set-up vs set-up-wrong). PRD PROF-2 'status' field is unspecified so PRD does not adjudicate.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §5: pick one canonical ExecutionProfile enum (recommend the DATA_MODEL §4.8 / UX §8.8 set since it carries the operationally-needed `active`/`in_use`/`unknown`), explicitly map or drop SOM §15's `ready`→`available`, `not_configured`→`misconfigured`, and decide the fate of SOM `degraded`. Update the DATA_MODEL §4.8 citation so it no longer falsely claims to equal SOM §15.

findings.finding: AgentTeam has a full 9-state lifecycle in SOM §14 and is required by MVP-present surfaces (proj_project_activity.active_teams counter, ProjectGraph `agent_team` node, OBS-2, attention sorting), yet it is NOT one of 'the 8 state machines' in DATA_MODEL §4 and has no persisted status column or projection. The draft defers Agent Team *orchestration* to P1 (§18.2) but TEAM-1 mandates modeling teams in MVP, and the activity counter cannot be computed without a team status.
findings.evidence: SOM §14 (719-727): draft, starting, active, waiting_on_human, blocked, reconciling_outputs, completed, failed, archived (9 states, with events AgentTeam* in SOM §14 / EM §10.11). DATA_MODEL §2.3 proj_project_activity has `active_teams INTEGER` (line 121) which requires knowing per-team status. proj_session has `agent_team_id` (line 131) but there is no `proj_agent_team` projection or `agent_teams` registry table anywhere in DATA_MODEL §2. PRD TEAM-1 (line 1295): 'MUST model agent teams even if full team orchestration is P1.' UX graph node `Agent Team` + `Team lead`/`Orchestrator`/`Worker` (Screen 3 lines 794-798) are MVP graph nodes.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §5: add AgentTeam as a state machine (even if MVP only exercises draft/active/completed/archived) with a minimal `agent_teams` registry row or `proj_agent_team` projection carrying status, so active_teams is derivable and graph nodes have a status. Document which states are MVP-live vs P1-dormant. Note the `waiting_on_human`/`blocked` overlap with Session waiting states for attention-ordering.

findings.finding: WorkflowPersonalizationRun has a 10-state lifecycle in SOM §18 that drives Flow C / Screen 13 (the personalization approval flow) and is referenced by workflow_instances.personalization_run_id, but it has NO state machine in DATA_MODEL §4 and nowhere to persist its granular states. The WorkflowInstance machine only exposes the single coarse state `personalization_in_progress`, collapsing 6 distinct run sub-states the UX needs.
findings.evidence: SOM §18 (953-962): draft, scanning, awaiting_answers, plan_ready, awaiting_approval, writing_files, review_ready, completed, failed, cancelled — with events WorkflowPersonalization* (SOM §18) / EM §10.3 WorkflowInstancePersonalization*. DATA_MODEL §2.8 workflow_instances has `personalization_run_id TEXT` (line 381) FK-ish reference but there is no personalization_runs table and no §4 machine. UX Screen 13 'Workflow Personalization Review' has an explicit stepper with two approval pauses (UX lines 1534-1537: 'Approve generation plan' / 'Review generated files') that map exactly to SOM `plan_ready`/`awaiting_approval` and `review_ready` — these cannot be rendered from a single `personalization_in_progress` instance state. AG §19.2 also specifies the personalization flow's intermediate gates.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §5/§13: either (a) add WorkflowPersonalizationRun as a persisted object with its SOM §18 state machine (table + status), or (b) explicitly DEFER it to P1 alongside the personalization UI and document that MVP collapses it to the single WorkflowInstance `personalization_in_progress` — but if deferred, also flag that Screen 13 / Flow C are P1 (the draft §18.2 already defers 'full cc-crew personalization UI', so option (b) is consistent — just make the state-machine deferral explicit).

findings.finding: WorkflowInstance machine: DATA_MODEL §4.5 / UX §8.5 dropped SOM §17's `running` state and renamed `ready_for_team_run`→`ready_for_team_mode`, while adding `not_detected, pack_available, generated_review_required, degraded`. An instance that is actively executing a team run now has no representable state (it would be stuck at `active` or `ready_for_team_mode`), and the rename is unreconciled.
findings.evidence: SOM §17 (893-902): detected, needs_personalization, personalization_in_progress, active, ready_for_team_run, RUNNING, drift_detected, upgrade_available, archived, detached. DATA_MODEL §4.5 (line 508) / UX §8.5 (584-597): not_detected, pack_available, needs_personalization, personalization_in_progress, generated_review_required, active, ready_for_team_MODE, degraded, drift_detected, upgrade_available, archived, detached — `running` is gone, `ready_for_team_run`≠`ready_for_team_mode`. PRD WF-3 (1346-1362) lists: available, installed, detected, needs_personalization, personalization_in_progress, generated_review_required, active, ready_for_team_run, degraded, drift_detected, upgrade_available, archived, detached — PRD uses `ready_for_team_run` (matching SOM) AND has `available/installed` (Pack states leaking into Instance). Three-way token drift.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §5: reconcile to one canonical WorkflowInstance enum. Decide `ready_for_team_run` vs `ready_for_team_mode` (PRD+SOM say _run). Decide whether `running` is needed (a team-run-in-progress state) or whether team-run status lives on AgentTeam instead (recommended: keep instance at `active`, track run on AgentTeam — but then say so). Separate Pack-level states (available/installed) from Instance-level states (PRD WF-3 conflates them).

findings.finding: Worktree machine (DERIVED from live git2) mixes git-readable states with lifecycle/lease/event states that are NOT derivable from a git status read, with no rule for how the derived `status` is computed when multiple conditions hold simultaneously. The count drift (UX §8.3=11 omits `creating`; SOM §7 / DATA_MODEL §4.3 / =12) is the surface symptom; the deeper gap is undefined precedence and non-derivability.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL §4.3 (line 501-502) declares Worktree status DERIVED 'from live git2 read + event hints' but the enum {creating, clean, dirty, untracked_files, conflicts, behind_base, ahead_of_base, pr_open, merged, prunable, locked, deleted} mixes orthogonal axes: git2 CAN read dirty/untracked/conflicts/ahead/behind; git2 CANNOT alone determine `creating` (in-flight worktree-add action), `locked` (a leases-table fact, §2.6), `pr_open`/`merged` (GitHub-synced, §4.4 PR machine), `prunable` (heuristic), `deleted` (event). A real worktree is simultaneously e.g. dirty+ahead_of_base+pr_open — the spec gives no precedence to collapse these into one `status` string. UX §8.3 (11, no `creating`) vs SOM §7/DATA_MODEL §4.3 (12, with `creating`) is the visible drift. PRD GIT-3 (1201-1213)=11 (matches UX).
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §5/§7: split Worktree into (a) a derived git sync-state (clean|dirty|untracked|conflicts|ahead|behind) read live from git2, and (b) a lifecycle/overlay state (creating|locked|pr_open|merged|prunable|deleted) sourced from events/leases/PR-sync. Define the precedence function that produces the single display `status` (e.g. locked/conflicts > dirty > ahead/behind > clean). Reconcile the enum to include `creating` everywhere or define it as a transient action state not a worktree status.

findings.finding: Time-derived `stale` is defined ONLY for Session; the same staleness/heartbeat-aging concept is needed by AgentTeam, ProjectBrain (`stale`/`reindex_required`), ExecutionProfile, IntegrationConnection, and ImplementationPlan (`stale`/`out_of_sync`) but no general time-derived-transition rule exists, and the Session `stale` threshold is unspecified.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL §4.1 (line 496): 'stale is derived by the daemon when now - last_heartbeat_at > threshold (no event needed — a time-derived transition)' — but the threshold value is never given (OQ has no row for it). SOM §10 ImplementationPlan has `stale`/`out_of_sync`, SOM §23 ProjectBrain has `stale`+`reindex_required`, SOM §24 MemorySource has `stale`, SOM §25 EvidenceItem has `stale`, SOM §33 IntegrationConnection lifecycle — none of these have a defined derivation trigger or staleness clock. proj_session.last_heartbeat_at exists (line 147) but proj_worktree.git_checked_at (line 190) staleness has no transition either. PRD §14.7 'Degraded States' requires showing 'Project Brain stale' / 'execution profile offline' / 'session usage unavailable' — all time/liveness-derived with no machine.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §7 (source-of-truth / staleness): define a general 'time-derived / liveness-derived transition' rule: per-object staleness clock, threshold, and whether the transition emits an event or is pure-read-time derivation. Specify the Session `stale` threshold (e.g. heartbeat-age > N×refreshInterval) and apply the same pattern to Brain `stale`/`reindex_required`, ExecutionProfile liveness, and the git-cache `git_checked_at`. List the staleness thresholds as configurable policy.

findings.finding: Illegal-transition handling is asserted but underspecified: DATA_MODEL §4 preamble says illegal transitions 'emit a degraded-state marker (EM §22/§23) not a silent overwrite', but no state machine defines its LEGAL transition set, so 'illegal' is undefined. The projector cannot validate transitions it was never given.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL §4 (line 493): 'transitions are driven by events and validated by the projector (illegal transitions emit a degraded-state marker ... not a silent overwrite).' But §4.1-§4.8 list only the SET of states, never the allowed edges (e.g. can a session go completed→active? killed→active? archived→anything?). EM §23 failure table (line 1537) only covers 'Unknown event type' / 'Corrupt payload', not 'event implies illegal state transition'. The terminal states (failed/completed/archived/killed for Session; merged/closed/abandoned for Task; merged/closed for PR) have no stated immutability rule — nothing says archived is terminal-absorbing.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §5: for each of the (now 9-10) machines, specify the legal transition edges and the terminal/absorbing states, OR at minimum the terminal-state set + the rule that any event implying an out-of-set transition is logged as a projection-degraded marker per EM §23. Add a row to EM §23 failure modes for 'event implies illegal transition'. This is required for the projector validation the draft promises to be testable (§14 'illegal-transition' is not in the test list).

findings.finding: Session waiting-state naming drift: DATA_MODEL §4.1 + SOM §12 + EM use `waiting_on_human_input` while PRD SESS-3 + EM §10.9 event use `waiting_on_human` / `SessionWaitingOnHuman`. Minor token mismatch that will surface as an enum/event-name inconsistency in the projector.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL §4.1 (line 496) & SOM §12 (line 603): `waiting_on_human_input`. PRD SESS-3 (line 948): `waiting_on_human`. EM §10.9 event (line 713): `SessionWaitingOnHuman`. proj_project_activity comment (line 117) uses 'waiting_on_permission|human|external' (abbreviated). The state token and the event token disagree (`waiting_on_human_input` state vs `SessionWaitingOnHuman` event).
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §5: pick one canonical token (recommend `waiting_on_human_input` for the status to disambiguate from `waiting_on_human_clarification` in UX Screen 5 line 976) and make the event name consistent (`SessionWaitingOnHumanInput`). Apply across SOM/UX/DATA_MODEL/EM.

findings.finding: Task vs PlanTask: a single shared state machine (DATA_MODEL §4.2) is asserted, but SOM §9 (Task) and SOM §11 (PlanTask) define DIFFERENT enums, and the draft itself flags the unification as OPEN (OQ-DATA-7). The §4.2 machine silently picked SOM §9's Task enum and dropped SOM §11's PlanTask states (not_started/ready/in_review/done/deferred/trimmed/out_of_sync), which the Plan View renders.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL §4.2 (line 499) uses SOM §9 Task enum: unassigned→queued→assigned→in_progress; blocked|needs_clarification; changes_ready→pr_opened→needs_review→requested_changes; merged|closed|abandoned. SOM §11 PlanTask (519-528) is DIFFERENT: not_started, ready, blocked, in_progress, in_review, done, deferred, trimmed, out_of_sync. UX Screen 7 Plan View + PRD §10.8 PLAN-3 use plan-task semantics (status with `done`/`deferred`), not Task semantics (`merged`/`abandoned`). DATA_MODEL §4.2 explicitly notes 'Open: whether Task and PlanTask share one machine' (line 499) and OQ-DATA-7 marks it MVP-blocking-OPEN — so this is acknowledged but unresolved.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §5: resolve OQ-DATA-7. If one machine: define the superset enum and the source-specific subsets each surface uses (Plan View shows {not_started,ready,in_progress,in_review,done,deferred} mapped from the unified set). If two machines: give PlanTask its own SOM §11 machine bound to proj_plan_progress.status (currently §4.2 forces the Task enum onto proj_plan_progress, line 201, which is wrong for plan semantics).
